flashcards.q: Explain "composition over configuration" and its key tradeoff.
flashcards.a: Instead of a component with an ever-growing prop surface (configuration), break it into smaller composable pieces consumers assemble directly. Tradeoff: composition pushes more responsibility/code onto the consumer for simple cases -- the wrong choice for genuinely uniform, common-case components.

flashcards.q: How do compound components (e.g. Tabs.List/Tab/Panel) share state without prop drilling?
flashcards.a: React Context scoped to the compound component -- the parent holds shared state and provides it via context; children consume it internally. The consumer still fully controls DOM structure/arrangement, unlike a monolithic prop-driven API.

flashcards.q: What is the W3C DTCG design token standard and what problem does it solve?
flashcards.a: First stable spec published October 2025, standardizing token shape via $value/$type. Solves per-tool format fragmentation -- before it, translating a token from Figma to Style Dictionary to CSS/JS output was a manual, error-prone, drift-prone process; now major tools (Figma, Style Dictionary v4+) support the format directly.

flashcards.q: Why must components reference semantic tokens, never primitive tokens directly, for theming to work?
flashcards.a: A theme is just a different semantic-to-primitive mapping (color.background.primary -> gray.50 in light, gray.900 in dark). A component hardcoding a primitive token bypasses that indirection entirely, which is the most common real bug that breaks theming.

flashcards.q: Why is versioning a design system genuinely harder than versioning a typical utility library?
flashcards.a: Semver assumes the public surface equals the code API, but a token rename or value change can silently break visual output across dozens of consuming surfaces with zero code API change -- it looks like a safe patch/minor bump by code rules while behaving like a breaking change for consumers relying on prior visual output.

flashcards.q: What should a mature team do differently before shipping a token value change, versus treating it as a routine patch?
flashcards.a: Run visual regression across the WHOLE system (not just the "obviously" changed component) and treat token renames/value changes with deprecation rigor comparable to an API breaking change, not an automatic patch bump.

flashcards.q: When is building a formal design system premature?
flashcards.a: For a single product with one team and no concrete near-term plan for a second consuming surface -- the coordination overhead (versioned package, cross-team review, deprecation policy) only pays off once genuine reuse across multiple consumers exists.

flashcards.q: Compare headless/behavior-only component libraries (Radix, React Aria) vs fully styled opinionated ones (Material UI, Chakra).
flashcards.a: Headless: correct ARIA/keyboard logic solved once, zero visual opinion, more setup per consuming team, best for strong brand differentiation needs. Fully styled: fastest to a consistent functional UI, but fights against distinctive visual differentiation since its value proposition IS the consistent default look.

flashcards.q: What does it indicate when most consuming teams regularly override a component via an open style/className prop rather than using its defined variants?
flashcards.a: The variant system hasn't actually captured the real design space needed -- the system provides an illusion of consistency that's silently bypassed, arguably worse than visible inconsistency since the override usually isn't caught in review.

flashcards.q: What does token aliasing (e.g. {color.blue.500}) enable in the DTCG format?
flashcards.a: A semantic token's $value can reference a primitive token by path, letting the primitive change (rebrand, palette adjustment) without touching every place that referenced the semantic name -- the mechanism theming and single-sourcing depend on.

flashcards.q: How do design systems ship a breaking prop rename across hundreds of call sites without a coordinated big-bang migration?
flashcards.a: A codemod (an automated AST transformation, commonly jscodeshift) rewrites consuming code from the old shape to the new one mechanically, published with the new major version so each team migrates on its own schedule; a deprecation window supporting the old prop with a console warning decouples release from full migration.

flashcards.q: Beyond sentiment, what are concrete metrics for measuring design system success?
flashcards.a: % of UI built from system components vs custom one-offs (via static import analysis), frequency/size of style-prop escape-hatch usage (rising trend = eroding fit), time-to-ship vs pre-system baseline, and for federated systems, the ratio of external-team contributions to core-team contributions.
